accepted.s: The inscription on the Mehrauli iron pillar refers to the king by which name?
accepted.x: The inscription refers to the ruler as ‘Chandra’, generally identified with Chandragupta II.
accepted.tq: Use the exact name in the inscription rather than the ruler’s full conventional name.
accepted.sec: Mehrauli iron pillar - location, ruler, metallurgy

accepted.s:
With reference to the Mehrauli iron pillar, consider the following statements:
1. It is presently located at Mehrauli in Delhi.
2. It was originally set up at Udayagiri near Vidisha.
3. Its inscription claims the king’s authority over parts of North-West India and Bengal.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The pillar is now at Mehrauli, was originally erected at Udayagiri near Vidisha, and its inscription records victories or authority in the North-West and Bengal.
accepted.tq: Link present location, original location and inscriptional claim without confusing Delhi with Vidisha.
accepted.sec: Mehrauli iron pillar - location, ruler, metallurgy

accepted.s: The exceptional resistance of the Mehrauli iron pillar to rust is mainly associated with which feature of its iron composition?
o: High phosphorus content forming a protective layer
Complete absence of carbon in the iron
accepted.x: The high-phosphorus iron is associated with the formation of a protective layer, helping the pillar resist corrosion for more than fifteen centuries.
accepted.tq: Identify the material property that explains the observed historical result.
accepted.sec: Mehrauli iron pillar - location, ruler, metallurgy

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Sarnath school of Gupta sculpture?
o: Polished buff sandstone images with a restrained treatment of ornament
Highly ornamented images carved mainly in black basalt
Bronze images with elaborate royal costumes
Granite images depicting only Hindu deities
accepted.x: Sarnath sculpture used polished Chunar buff sandstone and generally avoided heavy ornamentation.
accepted.tq: Separate Sarnath’s material and restrained style from Mathura and metal sculpture.
accepted.sec: Sculpture - Sarnath, Mathura, Sultanganj Buddhas

accepted.s: The seated Buddha images of the Sarnath school are especially associated with which mudra?
accepted.x: The seated Buddha at Sarnath is characteristically shown in the Dharmachakra mudra, symbolising the turning of the wheel of the Dharma.
accepted.tq: Test the distinctive iconographic attribute associated with a specific school.
accepted.sec: Sculpture - Sarnath, Mathura, Sultanganj Buddhas

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements about Gupta-period sculpture is correct?
1. Gupta stone sculpture grew out of the Mathura school.
2. The Sultanganj Buddha is a bronze image more than two metres high.
3. The Sarnath Buddha is shown with a thin clinging robe covering both shoulders.
4. The halo of Sarnath Buddha images may contain floral carving.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. Gupta sculpture developed from the Mathura tradition, while the Sultanganj bronze and Sarnath images display the stated features.
accepted.tq: Check each statement against the school, material, clothing and halo features.
accepted.sec: Sculpture - Sarnath, Mathura, Sultanganj Buddhas

accepted.s: The Sultanganj Buddha, regarded as a major Gupta metal image, is located in relation to which place and material?
accepted.x: The Sultanganj Buddha is a bronze image from the Bhagalpur region of Bihar and is over two metres high.
accepted.tq: Pair the monument with its location and material.
accepted.sec: Sculpture - Sarnath, Mathura, Sultanganj Buddhas

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Bamiyan Buddhas — Gupta period
2. Eran Varaha — Vaishnava presence
3. Sarnath images — Dharmachakra mudra
4. Sultanganj Buddha — bronze image
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Bamiyan Buddhas are assigned to the Gupta period, Eran Varaha indicates Vaishnava presence, Sarnath is associated with Dharmachakra mudra, and Sultanganj is a bronze Buddha.
accepted.tq: Verify each monument through its period, religious association, iconography or material.
accepted.sec: Sculpture - Sarnath, Mathura, Sultanganj Buddhas

accepted.s: Which one of the following Gupta temples is correctly matched with its location?
o: Bhitargaon — Satna district of Madhya Pradesh
Bhumara Shiva temple — Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh
Tigawa — Katni region of Madhya Pradesh
accepted.x: Tigawa is located in the Katni region, formerly associated with Jabalpur, in Madhya Pradesh. Bhitargaon is in Kanpur, Bhumara in Satna, and Dashavatara at Deogarh near Lalitpur.
accepted.tq: Use location swaps as the principal trap in temple questions.
accepted.sec: Gupta temples → place + material

accepted.s: Which one of the following temples is built of brick and is associated with an early shikhara?
accepted.x: The Bhitargaon temple in Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh, is a brick Gupta temple associated with an early shikhara.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the sole brick example from the stone temples in the group.
accepted.sec: Gupta temples → place + material

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below the lists.
List-I (Temple)
a. Temple 17, Sanchi
b. Parvati temple, Nachna
c. Shiva temple, Bhumara
d. Dashavatara temple, Deogarh
List-II (Feature)
i. Two flanking shrines at the entrance
ii. Covered ambulatory and two-storeyed structure
iii. Flat roof and four-pillar porch
iv. Shikhara and panchayatana plan
accepted.x: Sanchi 17 has a flat roof and four-pillar porch; Nachna has a covered ambulatory; Bhumara has flanking shrines; and Deogarh has a shikhara with a panchayatana plan.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure architectural features and eliminate codes containing a mismatched temple.
accepted.sec: Gupta temples → place + material

accepted.s:
Arrange the following stages of Gupta temple architecture in chronological order:
A. Low square shikhara and high platform
B. Square sanctum with flat roof and shallow porch
C. Covered ambulatory with raised platform
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Stage 1 had a square sanctum and flat roof; Stage 2 introduced the covered ambulatory and raised platform; Stage 3 developed the low square shikhara and high platform.
accepted.tq: Identify the architectural progression from flat-roofed forms to shikhara forms.
accepted.sec: Gupta temples → place + material

accepted.s: The Gupta period is significant in temple architecture because it marks the shift from
o: Nagara temples to purely Buddhist viharas
rock-cut forms to free-standing structural temples
accepted.x: The Gupta age marks an important transition from rock-cut architecture to free-standing structural temples.
accepted.tq: Test the direction of change rather than merely naming the period.
accepted.sec: Gupta temples → place + material

accepted.s: Gupta silver coins introduced after the conquest of the Western Kshatrapas were modelled on
accepted.x: The silver coins introduced after the Saka conquest were modelled on Saka silver issues.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the model of the silver issues from the materials and coinage of other dynasties.
accepted.sec: Gupta coinage - dinara, silver after Saka conquest, coin types

accepted.s: Which one of the following coin types is correctly associated with its Gupta ruler?
o: Kartikeya feeding peacock type — Chandragupta II
accepted.x: The veena-player or lyrist type was issued by Samudragupta. The king-queen type belongs to Chandragupta I, the archer type to Chandragupta II, and the Kartikeya-peacock type to Kumaragupta I.
accepted.tq: Use ruler–coin-type associations and reject swapped rulers.
accepted.sec: Gupta coinage - dinara, silver after Saka conquest, coin types

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below the lists.
List-I (Coin type)
a. King-queen
b. Tiger-slayer
c. Lion-slayer
d. Garuda standard
List-II (Ruler)
i. Chandragupta I
ii. Samudragupta
iii. Chandragupta II
iv. Skandagupta
accepted.x: The king-queen type belongs to Chandragupta I; tiger-slayer to Samudragupta; lion-slayer to Chandragupta II; and Garuda standard to Skandagupta.
accepted.tq: Start with the distinctive king-queen and lion-slayer types, then complete the code.
accepted.sec: Gupta coinage - dinara, silver after Saka conquest, coin types

accepted.s: Which of the following coin types is associated with Kumaragupta I?
o: Kartikeya or king feeding a peacock and Ashvamedha
accepted.x: Kumaragupta I issued coins depicting Kartikeya or the king feeding a peacock, as well as Ashvamedha coins.
accepted.tq: Test the ruler associated with a distinctive iconographic coin type.
accepted.sec: Gupta coinage - dinara, silver after Saka conquest, coin types

accepted.s: The Bagh caves are best described as
o: nine Buddhist viharas in Dhar district, with paintings having secular and local themes
twenty Hindu caves at Vidisha, all devoted to Vishnu
a group of Jain caves at Odisha associated with Kharavela
a group of royal Gupta temples constructed entirely of brick
accepted.x: The Bagh caves in Dhar district of Madhya Pradesh comprise nine Buddhist viharas, generally dated to the fifth–sixth centuries CE, and their paintings include secular and local themes.
accepted.tq: Combine cave number, religious function, location and painting character.
accepted.sec: Bagh and other caves - Hallisaka, Udayagiri Varaha, Buddhist caves

accepted.s: The Hallisaka painting at Bagh caves depicts
accepted.x: The Hallisaka painting at Bagh is known for depicting a joyous folk dance.
accepted.tq: Identify the subject of a named painting rather than its location alone.
accepted.sec: Bagh and other caves - Hallisaka, Udayagiri Varaha, Buddhist caves

accepted.s: The colossal Varaha panel at Udayagiri represents
accepted.x: The colossal Varaha at Udayagiri is a panel of Vishnu’s boar incarnation and reflects the Vaishnava orientation of the site.
accepted.tq: Use the deity–incarnation relationship to identify the sculpture.
accepted.sec: Bagh and other caves - Hallisaka, Udayagiri Varaha, Buddhist caves

accepted.s: Which inscriptional and historical association is connected with the Udayagiri caves?
o: Kharavela’s inscription recording the construction of Buddhist viharas
Virasena’s inscription recording the conquests of Chandragupta II
Ashoka’s edict recording the spread of Jainism
Rudradaman’s inscription recording the reign of Samudragupta
accepted.x: An inscription of Virasena at Udayagiri records the conquests of Chandragupta II.
accepted.tq: Match the inscription’s author with the ruler and site.
accepted.sec: Bagh and other caves - Hallisaka, Udayagiri Varaha, Buddhist caves

accepted.s:
Which one of the following is correctly matched?
1. Ellora Caves 1–12 — Buddhist group
2. Mandapeshwar — later Christian cave
3. Udayagiri near Vidisha — nineteen Hindu and one Jain cave
4. Bagh — five Buddhist viharas only
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Bagh had nine Buddhist viharas, not five, so statement 4 is false.
accepted.tq: Find the numerical distortion in an otherwise familiar list of cave complexes.
accepted.sec: Bagh and other caves - Hallisaka, Udayagiri Varaha, Buddhist caves

accepted.s:
The description of the Gupta period as a ‘Classical’ or ‘Golden’ age is supported by which of the following developments?
1. Peak of Sanskrit literature
2. Advances in mathematics and astronomy
3. Ajanta painting and Sarnath sculpture
4. Emergence of the first structural temples
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All four developments are cited as grounds for regarding the Gupta period as a classical age.
accepted.tq: Group the positive cultural and scientific indicators before checking the coded options.
accepted.sec: Classical age label - justification and criticism

accepted.s:
Which of the following is cited as a criticism of describing the Gupta period as a ‘Golden Age’?
1. Growth of land grants and feudatories
2. Expansion of vishti or forced labour
3. Decline of trade and towns
4. Falling status of women
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All four conditions are cited as limitations of the Golden Age label. The period’s prosperity and cultural achievements were not equally experienced by all sections of society.
accepted.tq: Contrast elite cultural achievement with social and economic criticisms.
accepted.sec: Classical age label - justification and criticism

accepted.s: The expression that the Gupta ‘Golden Age’ was mainly a golden age for the elite reflects which of the following conditions?
o: Permanent expansion of trade and towns
Rigid caste practices and unequal social benefits
Universal prosperity among peasants and labourers
accepted.x: The criticism highlights rigid caste distinctions, forced labour, declining trade and towns, and the falling status of women, showing that benefits were unevenly distributed.
accepted.tq: Apply the criticism of an historical label to its social implications.
accepted.sec: Classical age label - justification and criticism

accepted.s: Which of the following is correctly classified as a Mahakavya of Kalidasa?
accepted.x: Raghuvamsha is a Mahakavya of Kalidasa. Meghaduta and Ritusamhara are lyric poems, while Malavikagnimitram is a drama.
accepted.tq: Separate Kalidasa’s dramas, epics and lyric poems by genre.
accepted.sec: Kalidasa - dramas vs poems, plots, wrong attributions

accepted.s:

List-I (Work)
a. Abhijnana Shakuntalam
b. Vikramorvashiyam
c. Kumarasambhava
d. Meghaduta
List-II (Genre)
i. Mahakavya
ii. Drama
iii. Lyric poem
iv. Drama
accepted.x: Abhijnana Shakuntalam and Vikramorvashiyam are dramas; Kumarasambhava is a Mahakavya; and Meghaduta is a lyric poem.
accepted.tq: Classify each work by genre before selecting the matching code.
accepted.sec: Kalidasa - dramas vs poems, plots, wrong attributions

accepted.s: Malavikagnimitram centres on the love of Agnimitra and Malavika. Agnimitra was a
accepted.x: Malavikagnimitram portrays the love of Agnimitra, a Shunga king of Vidisha, and Malavika.
accepted.tq: Use the plot to identify the historical ruler and dynasty.
accepted.sec: Kalidasa - dramas vs poems, plots, wrong attributions

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: Shringara Shataka is attributed to Bhartrihari, not Kalidasa. Kiratarjuniyam, Shishupalavadha and Naishadhiyacharita are associated with Bharavi, Magha and Sriharsha respectively.
accepted.tq: Detect the deliberate wrong attribution among works commonly grouped with classical Sanskrit literature.
accepted.sec: Kalidasa - dramas vs poems, plots, wrong attributions

accepted.s: Which of the following works is associated with a post-Gupta author rather than Kalidasa?
accepted.x: Naishadhiyacharita was written by Sriharsha, who belongs to the post-Gupta period. The other three works are associated with Kalidasa.
accepted.tq: Separate works of Kalidasa from later Sanskrit mahakavyas through author attribution.
accepted.sec: Kalidasa - dramas vs poems, plots, wrong attributions
